skill.name: haskell-pro
skill.description: Expert Haskell guidance for advanced types, pure architecture, concurrency, parsing, testing, performance, and project structure.
skill.summary: Design and improve maintainable Haskell systems with strong types and explicit effects.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: Complex Haskell designs can hide unsafe assumptions, unclear effects, and performance problems. This skill provides practical guidance for typed architecture, concurrency, parsing, testing, and builds.
actual_capabilities: Design domain models with GADTs, newtypes, type families, and phantom types.
Recommend total functions and isolate effects behind explicit boundaries.
Structure Cabal or Stack projects with clear modules and dependency hygiene.
Develop STM and async concurrency patterns with exception-safe resource handling.
Guide parsing and serialization with Megaparsec and Aeson.
Create QuickCheck and Hspec tests based on properties and invariants.
limitations: The skill does not run GHC, Cabal, Stack, profilers, or test suites by itself.
Recommendations require validation against the project compiler version and dependencies.
Performance guidance depends on real profiling data and representative workloads.
The skill does not replace project-specific security or production review.

use_cases.title: Model a New Domain
use_cases.description: Turn business rules into explicit types, validated constructors, and pure transformations.
use_cases.target_user: Haskell developers designing a new service or library

use_cases.title: Review Concurrent Code
use_cases.description: Assess STM, async, cancellation, and exception handling for clear ownership and reliable behavior.
use_cases.target_user: Senior engineers reviewing concurrent Haskell systems

use_cases.title: Strengthen a Haskell Project
use_cases.description: Improve module boundaries, build configuration, parsing, tests, and dependency practices.
use_cases.target_user: Teams maintaining an existing Cabal or Stack project

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Function
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain and improve this Haskell function: [paste function]. Identify partial behavior, clarify its type signature, and propose focused tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small function

prompt_templates.title: Design a Typed Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Model these domain rules in Haskell: [rules]. Use the simplest types that prevent invalid states and explain each design decision.

prompt_templates.title: Review Concurrent Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this concurrent Haskell design: [description or code]. Analyze STM boundaries, cancellation, exceptions, resource cleanup, and test strategy.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Production Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged refactor plan for this Haskell project: [context]. Address module design, effects, dependencies, profiling, compatibility, migration risks, and verification.

output_examples.input: Review a parser that mixes validation, file access, and error formatting.
output_examples.output: The response separates pure parsing from file access, recommends typed errors, identifies partial cases, and proposes parser properties.

output_examples.input: Design an order workflow that prevents payment before validation.
output_examples.output: The response models workflow states with distinct types, limits valid transitions, explains constructor visibility, and outlines property-based tests.

output_examples.input: Investigate unstable latency in an STM worker system.
output_examples.output: The response requests profiling evidence, reviews transaction size and contention, checks cancellation behavior, and defines measurable verification steps.

best_practices: Provide compiler version, dependency versions, constraints, and expected behavior.
Include minimal relevant code and exact build, test, or profiling errors.
Validate recommendations with compilation, tests, benchmarks, and representative workloads.
anti_patterns: Do not request advanced type features without a concrete invariant or maintenance benefit.
Do not optimize from source inspection alone when profiling data is available.
Do not apply generated changes without checking compiler compatibility and project tests.

faq.question: Which Haskell topics does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers type systems, pure architecture, concurrency, parsing, effects, performance, builds, dependency hygiene, and testing.

faq.question: Can it help with Cabal and Stack projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review project structure, dependencies, module organization, and build configuration for either tool.

faq.question: Does it execute or compile Haskell code?
faq.answer: No. Tool execution depends on the agent environment and user authorization.

faq.question: Can it diagnose performance problems?
faq.answer: It can interpret profiling evidence and suggest strictness, allocation, fusion, or concurrency improvements. Final decisions require benchmarks.

faq.question: Can it create tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose Hspec examples, QuickCheck properties, invariants, and edge cases.

faq.question: When should I use another skill?
faq.answer: Use another skill when the task is outside Haskell or requires specialized infrastructure, security, or deployment expertise.
